name: Kerr Rotating Black Hole
description: The exact vacuum solution for a rotating, uncharged black hole, characterized by mass and angular momentum. It features an ergosphere, frame dragging, and a ring singularity, and describes essentially all astrophysical black holes.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ and $G$ explicit, and the two parameters are the mass $M$ and the spin per unit mass $a = J/(Mc)$, which carries dimensions of length. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: For nearly half a century after Schwarzschild, the rotating case resisted everyone. Schwarzschild's 1916 solution described a static, spherical mass, but real stars spin, and the search for the exterior field of a rotating body became one of the notorious unsolved problems of general relativity, attempted and abandoned by a generation of relativists. One exact stationary vacuum field with rotational symmetry did turn up, Achilles Papapetrou's of 1953, and it has angular momentum but no mass [papapetrou1953, dautcourt2009]. The breakthrough came in 1963 from Roy Kerr, a New Zealander then at the University of Texas, who found it by restricting attention to metrics of a special algebraic type and letting that structure guide him to the answer, where brute force had failed [kerr1963]. The paper is two pages long. Its solution is, by a common reckoning, the most important exact solution ever found to Einstein's equations.¶Kerr had come to Austin at the invitation of Alfred Schild, and it was with Schild watching from an armchair in his office that Kerr computed the angular momentum of the new metric and found that it describes a spinning body [kerr2009]. In his haste he got the sign of the rotation parameter wrong, which is why the sign of $a$ in the 1963 paper differs from that in every later one [kerr2009]. He presented the solution at the first Texas Symposium on Relativistic Astrophysics, held in Dallas from 16 to 18 December 1963 to find an explanation for the newly discovered quasars [kerr2009].¶The geometry Kerr uncovered is far richer than Schwarzschild's. A rotating black hole drags spacetime around with it, so inertial frames near the hole are swept along in the direction of spin, and this frame dragging becomes inescapable inside a region called the ergosphere, where nothing can remain at rest relative to the distant stars. The solution has two horizons, an outer and an inner, and at its core the point singularity of Schwarzschild is stretched into a ring. Others made much of this structure clear only later: in 1967 Robert Boyer and Richard Lindquist gave the coordinates now universally used to write the metric and built its maximal analytic extension [boyer1967], and in 1968 Brandon Carter discovered a hidden constant of motion that renders the geodesic equations integrable, so that orbits around a Kerr hole can be solved exactly [carter1968]. Carter found the price of the extension as well: in every case but the spherical one the extended geometry contains closed timelike lines, and the only geodesics that reach the ring singularity lie in its equatorial plane [carter1968]. Carl Sagan ruled that extension out as a route between the stars in Contact, where Eda, one of the travellers, explains that the exact Kerr solution has an interior tunnel but that it is unstable, the slightest perturbation sealing it off into a singularity through which nothing can pass [sagan1985].¶The ergosphere stores energy that can be drawn out. In 1969 Roger Penrose showed that a particle entering it can split so that one fragment falls in carrying negative energy while the other escapes with more energy than the original possessed, energy mined directly from the hole's rotation [penrose1969]. Roger Blandford and Roman Znajek showed in 1977 that magnetic field lines threading a spinning black hole can carry off its energy and angular momentum electromagnetically, and proposed the mechanism as the engine of active galactic nuclei [blandford1977].¶Saul Teukolsky found in 1972 that the gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations of a Kerr black hole obey wave equations that separate completely [teukolsky1972, teukolsky1973], and with William Press he used them in 1973 to test the hole's stability, finding no unstable mode for any spin, even close to the extreme [press1973]. Uniqueness theorems establish that an isolated, stationary black hole in our universe is characterized entirely by its mass and spin, which is to say that it is a Kerr black hole. Werner Israel proved in 1967 that the only static black hole is Schwarzschild's [israel1967], Brandon Carter showed in 1971 that an axisymmetric black hole has only two degrees of freedom, its mass and its angular momentum [carter1971], Stephen Hawking showed in 1972 that a stationary black hole that rotates must be axisymmetric [hawking1972], and David Robinson completed the argument in 1975 by proving the Kerr family the only one [robinson1975]. Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar closed his Nobel lecture of 1983 on this point: stationary, isolated black holes "are all, every single one of them, described exactly by the Kerr solution," which he called "the only instance we have of an exact description of a macroscopic object" [chandrasekhar1984].¶Kip Thorne and the visual effects team at Double Negative drew Gargantua, the black hole of Christopher Nolan's film Interstellar of 2014, by tracing bundles of light through the Kerr metric in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates, with its spin set at 0.6 of the maximum for the images although the story's time dilations need a hole spinning almost as fast as it can [nolan2014interstellar, james2015lensing]. The first detection of gravitational waves, on 14 September 2015, recorded two black holes of about 36 and 29 solar masses merging into one of 62 with a spin about two thirds of the maximum, the fading end of the signal matching a hole relaxing to a final stationary Kerr configuration [abbott2016]. The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration published the first image of a black hole's shadow in 2019, a ring 42 microarcseconds across at the core of the galaxy M87 around a mass of about 6.5 billion Suns, and found it consistent with the shadow of a Kerr black hole as general relativity predicts [eht2019]. Every quiescent black hole astronomers observe, from stellar remnants to the giants at the centers of galaxies, is described by the metric of those two pages of 1963.

related.text: Kerr's black hole with the spin switched off, $a = 0$. The horizon is a round sphere again and the ergosphere is gone.
Kerr's black hole given an electric charge to carry as it spins. At $r_Q = 0$ it is Kerr's metric.
A rotating black hole in three dimensions, with an outer and an inner horizon like Kerr's and the same curvature at every point [banados1992, banados1993].
A rotating wormhole with an ergoregion and no horizon. Its ergoregion is a tube round the equator of the throat, and the Penrose process draws energy from it as it does from Kerr's [teo1998].
Between the outer and inner horizons $r$ is a time, and with $t$ wrapped into a circle the region is a Gowdy spacetime on $S^2 \times S^1$ [obregon1998, garfinkle1999].

Kerr's metric with $\sqrt{r^2 + \ell^2}$ written for the Boyer-Lindquist radius and $dr$ left alone is the rotating black bounce of Mazza, Franzin, and Liberati, a regular black hole or a wormhole depending on $\ell$ [mazza2021].
Kerr's black hole in a universe with a cosmological constant of either sign. At $\Lambda = 0$ Carter's metric is Kerr's [carter1968separable].
Kerr's black hole in more than four dimensions, with a spin for every independent plane of rotation. From six dimensions up a hole turning in one plane keeps its horizon at every spin [myers1986].
Kerr spinning as fast as it can, seen from just outside the horizon. The region there is a throat without end, with four symmetries where Kerr has two [bardeen1999].

The field outside a slowly rotating star, to second order in its spin. The star's quadrupole moment is free, and at Kerr's value, $Q = J^2/M$, the field is Kerr's metric to that order [hartlethorne1968].

Kerr's black hole is a Malament-Hogarth spacetime. An observer falling to the inner horizon has by then received every signal a computer orbiting outside will ever send, however long it runs [etesi2002].

The charged black hole, which has an inner horizon as Kerr's does and spherical symmetry besides. Eric Poisson and Werner Israel took it in 1989 as a simple spherical model of the inside of a spinning hole, and found the mass within the inner horizon growing without bound [poisson1989, poisson1990].
Schwarzschild's metric with a twist $l$ where Kerr's has a spin $a$. Jerzy Plebański and Marek Demiański's family of 1976 holds both parameters at once [plebanski1976, griffiths2005].

The static field of a rod, which deforms Schwarzschild's metric by a quadrupole. Akira Tomimatsu and Humitaka Sato found a spinning vacuum solution in 1972 that is Kerr's metric at one value of its angular momentum and a Zipoy-Voorhees metric at none [tomimatsu1972, kodamahikida2003].

The static black hole of $D$ dimensions. Robert Myers and Malcolm Perry found its spinning family in 1986, the counterparts of Kerr's metric in higher dimensions, where a black hole can turn in several planes at once [myers1986, emparan2008].

A black hole with an acceleration where Kerr's has a spin. Jerzy Plebański and Marek Demiański put both into one family in 1976, and the spinning C-metric is Kerr's metric when the acceleration vanishes [plebanski1976, griffiths2005].

The throat of an extremal charged black hole, AdS$_2 \times$ S$^2$. James Bardeen and Gary Horowitz found in 1999 that the limit toward the horizon of an extreme Kerr black hole is its vacuum counterpart, with a timelike boundary at infinity as well [bardeen1999].

Kerr's metric with the mass taken out, $M = 0$, which is flat, in spheroidal coordinates built on a ring of radius $a$. Gary Gibbons and Mikhail Volkov pointed out in 2017 that the ring stays and joins two flat regions, so at $M = 0$ Kerr's spacetime is Minkowski space only locally [gibbons2017].

The shock wave of a black hole boosted to the speed of light. Valeria Ferrari and Paolo Pendenza boosted Kerr's along its axis in 1990, and took the limit to be the field of massless particles on a ring of radius $a$ [ferrari1990].

A star that shines. Prahlad Vaidya and L. K. Patel found a radiating Kerr metric in 1973, a field of flowing radiation with Kerr's symmetry that is Kerr's metric when the radiation is switched off [vaidya1973].

Two impulsive plane waves colliding. With their polarisations out of line the collision is Yavuz Nutku and Mustafa Halil's solution, which Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar and Valeria Ferrari derived in 1984 from the simplest solution of an equation of Ernst's type, as Kerr's metric is derived [chandrasekhar1984ferrari, nutku1977].

Schwarzschild's black hole with a cosmic string through it. Ruth Gregory, David Kubizňák, and Danielle Wills put the string through a Kerr black hole in 2013 and found its effect conical in a frame turning with the hole [gregory2013].

A charged spherical hole crossed by two streams of radiation, the model Eric Poisson and Werner Israel built in 1989 for the inside of a rotating one. Its mass function grows without limit at the inner horizon [poisson1989].
Kerr's black hole given a NUT parameter $l$ beside its spin. At $l = 0$ it is Kerr's metric, and for $|l| > |a|$ the ring singularity is gone [griffiths2005].

Two Kerr black holes on one axis, built by Dietrich Kramer and Gernot Neugebauer in 1980. The repulsion between the spins does not balance the attraction, and a strut on the axis between the holes holds them apart [kramer1980, neugebauer2009].
A cloud of rotating dust whose field far away is Kerr's frame dragging term alone: angular momentum with no mass [bonnor1977cloud, bratek2007].
A static magnet made from Kerr's metric. Bonnor's rule trades the twist of the spinning hole for a magnetic potential and turns $a^2$ into $-b^2$ [bonnor2002, davidson1994].
Kerr's hole with a rigidly rotating perfect fluid laid over it. Wahlquist's family in Mars's chart is Kerr's metric at $\beta = 0$, $\mu_0 = 0$, and $a_1 = 0$ [mars2001].
A spinning disc of dust whose outside field becomes Kerr's at $J = GM^2/c$ in the limit $\mu \to \mu_0$ of its one parameter, the disc itself shrinking to a point of Weyl's coordinates [meinel2002].

Two plane gravitational waves whose collision makes the inside of Kerr. Between their fronts the metric is Kerr's between its two horizons, with $t$ and $\phi$ running along the fronts and $\phi$ unrolled, and the waves end on the inner horizon [chandrasekhar1986, griffiths1991].
Kerr's black hole is two solitons on flat space. Belinski and Zakharov's inverse scattering method returns the Kerr-NUT solution from two poles, real ones for the hole with horizons [belinskii1979].

coordinates.name: Kerr (Boyer-Lindquist)

parameters.description: Spin per unit mass, $a = J/(Mc)$ with $J$ the angular momentum, carrying dimensions of length; a horizon exists only for $a \le GM/c^2$
Newton's constant, kept explicit along with $c$, so that the Schwarzschild radius appears throughout as $2GM/c^2$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates of Robert Boyer and Richard Lindquist, $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time. The horizons are at $r_\pm = GM/c^2 \pm \sqrt{G^2M^2/c^4 - a^2}$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\left(1 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}\right)c^2 dt^2 - \dfrac{4GMar\sin^2\theta}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}c\,dt\,d\phi + \dfrac{r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta}{r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}}dr^2 + \left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)d\theta^2 + \left(r^2 + a^2 + \dfrac{2GMa^2r\sin^2\theta}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}\right)\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2

nonzero.value: -\dfrac{GMa\sin\theta\cos\theta\left(3r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2 + a^2\sin^2\theta \left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}

\dfrac{GMa\sin\theta\cos\theta\left(3r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2 + a^2\sin^2\theta \left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}

\dfrac{GMa\sin\theta\cos\theta\left(3r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2 - a^2\sin^2\theta \left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}

-\dfrac{GMa\sin\theta\cos\theta\left(3r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2 - a^2\sin^2\theta \left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}

-\dfrac{GMa\sin\theta\cos\theta\left(3r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2 + a^2\sin^2\theta \left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}

\dfrac{GMa\sin\theta\cos\theta\left(3r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2 + a^2\sin^2\theta \left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}

\dfrac{GMa\sin\theta\cos\theta\left(3r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2 - a^2\sin^2\theta \left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}

-\dfrac{GMa\sin\theta\cos\theta\left(3r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(\left(r^2 + a^2\right)^2 - a^2\sin^2\theta \left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}

geodesics: \ddot{t} + \dfrac{2GM\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}\dot{t}\dot{r} - \dfrac{4GMa^2r\sin\theta\cos\theta}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2}\dot{t}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{2GMa\sin^2\theta\left(2r^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right) + \left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}\dot{r}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{4GMa^3r\sin^3\theta\cos\theta}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2}\dot{\theta}\dot{\phi} = 0

\ddot{r} + \dfrac{GM\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2GMa\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\sin^2\theta\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3}\dot{t}\dot{\phi} + \left(\dfrac{r}{r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta} - \dfrac{c^2r - GM}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}\right)\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{2a^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta}\dot{r}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{r\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}{r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)\sin^2\theta\left(c^2r\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2 - GMa^2\sin^2\theta\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

\ddot{\theta} - \dfrac{2GMa^2r\sin\theta\cos\theta}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{4GMar\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\sin\theta\cos\theta}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3}\dot{t}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{a^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}\dot{r}^2 + \dfrac{2r}{r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta}\dot{r}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{a^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\sin\theta\cos\theta\left(c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\right)\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2 + 2GMra^2\sin^2\theta\left(2r^2 + a^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^3}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

\ddot{\phi} + \dfrac{2GMa\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}\dot{t}\dot{r} - \dfrac{4GMar\cos\theta}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2\sin\theta}\dot{t}\dot{\theta} + 2\left(\dfrac{r}{r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta} - \dfrac{a^2\sin^2\theta\left(c^2r\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right) + GM\left(r^2 - a^2\cos^2\theta\right)\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2\left(r^2 + a^2 - \dfrac{2GMr}{c^2}\right)}\right)\dot{r}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{2\cos\theta\left(c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2 + 2GMra^2\sin^2\theta\right)}{c^2\left(r^2 + a^2\cos^2\theta\right)^2\sin\theta}\dot{\theta}\dot{\phi} = 0
